faults.title: Capture via silence
faults.text: The record cannot reach a person nobody wrote. An adversary need not falsify anything — only decline to record.
faults.book: Part V · Capture · Records and coordination

faults.title: The delivery gap
faults.text: Owed derives; delivered does not. Nothing in the record bakes bread.

faults.title: Authority ending and physical release
faults.text: Qualified relief can end custody authority. Review, release and continuity are duties; the record does not establish that an official honoured release.

faults.title: The valuation vacuum
faults.text: Contribution has no degree. Forty years of care and one week of auditing are the same word.

faults.title: A floor without a ballot
faults.text: The floor does not carry a vote; residence does. The boundary costs the newcomer and the former resident.
faults.book: Part V · Residence and political membership

faults.title: What a majority may not remove
faults.text: The floor and personhood cannot be amended away. The cost falls on a majority that wants to.
faults.book: Part V · What a majority may not remove

faults.title: Binary recognition: the Cira fork
faults.text: Adulthood evidence governs ballot eligibility. Missing evidence is not a punishment, and credentials do not become a transferable personal score.

faults.title: The audit only says “something is wrong”
faults.text: A reviewed defect withdraws a permission and lands duties. It does not make anyone move.
faults.book: Chapter 30 pins — “a formal duty, never proof that anybody acted”

faults.title: Conviction as the only housing route
faults.text: Custody establishes protection duties, not shelter. On the record the prisoner is no better housed than the child.

faults.title: “It can prove a citizen is starving”
faults.text: The design cannot tell you whether anyone is hungry. It can tell you nobody watched a meal arrive.

faults.title: “Innocent students lose their credentials”
faults.text: The clawback rule reaches Cira’s recognition and finds nothing there. Credentials were never involved; lose is a leaf.
faults.book: Chapter 26 — The Limits of a Finding

faults.title: The shield costs time
faults.text: A protected disclosure can block confinement under a recorded conviction while the connection is examined. Independent case findings require time and qualified reviewers.
faults.book: Part V · Capture · Protection while the connection is disputed

faults.title: Nobody staffs the night shift
faults.text: The design cannot conscript labour. When voluntary recruitment fails, a service goes unstaffed; the record shows the debt, not the nurse.

faults.title: One file per door
faults.text: Purpose-bound records cannot be reused. The cost falls on people who need several services and are recorded again at each.
faults.book: Part V · Capture · Records and coordination

faults.title: Delete one rule; the child is owed nothing
faults.text: Without the birth root, every duty still reads personhood — and personhood has nothing left to derive from.

faults.title: The firewall is dead
faults.text: Without “a prisoner is a person”, conviction closes the file: no debt survives to show a gap.
faults.book: Chapter 27 · A Prisoner Is a Person

faults.title: One signature, any signer
faults.text: An appointment route that skips the recall and carried-void checks hands the pen back to Vex and Boss.

faults.title: One line, and the shield goes
faults.text: The declared counterfactual removes the Court’s public entry. Compare protection and confinement conclusions on the same supplied record.

faults.title: Refusing work costs the exit
faults.text: One barrier deleted; its sibling stands. The hole is exactly the size of the line.

faults.title: Means-tested at the floor
faults.text: Without the floor gate, an economic factor may condition essentials. Payment still is not delivery.

faults.title: The receipt becomes the meal
faults.text: Remove one condition and the provider certifies its own delivery. This is why the condition exists.
